definition: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools, a model trained to decide which APIs to call, when to call them, what arguments to pass, and how to best incorporate the results.
details: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools, a model trained to decide which APIs to call, when to call them, what arguments to pass, and how to best incorporate the results.

explainer.lead: Toolformer is a model trained to teach itself to use tools: which APIs to call, when, with what arguments, and how to fold results back in. It matters because it lets a language model extend itself with external tools without hand-built pipelines.

tiers.eli5: Instead of memorizing everything, the model learns when to pick up a calculator or look something up, then uses the answer in its reply.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use the approach to let models decide tool calls and arguments on their own. A pitfall is trusting self-selected calls without checking that the arguments and results are sound.
tiers.paperLevel: The model learns to decide which APIs to call, when to call them, what arguments to pass, and how to incorporate the results. Limits come from the quality of the training signal for those decisions.

explainer.example: Asked a question needing arithmetic, the model inserts a calculator call with the operands, then uses the returned value in its answer.
